# OpenBot ### AI coworkers. Ready for the enterprise. A modular, self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers.
Choose your models. Bring your agents. Own your infrastructure. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) [Kubernetes](#deploy-on-kubernetes) [**OpenBot for Business · Get early access →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Docs**](docs/README.md) From [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), creators of [AG-UI](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui).
## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## See it in action https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/535ef7ee-1631-4a69-b839-564c56cf90b4 Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, review interactive results, and take over when it needs you. Teach it repeatable tasks through feedback and demonstrations. ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm chart deploys both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](charts/openbot/README.md) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. The chart installs Intelligence by default; no separate hosted project is required. For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with **amd64 nodes**, a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The commands below use an OpenAI key. For Anthropic, a model router, cluster sizing, or an existing Intelligence deployment, use the [full Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Give it this README and [the Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md). The guide covers cloud-specific values, storage, secrets, sign-in, networking, upgrades, and troubleshooting. Use the evaluation below only through a local port-forward; configure sign-in and TLS before sharing a deployment. 1. **Get the source.** Skip this if you already have a checkout. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` 2. **Create `openbot-secrets.yaml` locally.** Replace the placeholders with your license and model key. Keep this file out of source control. ```yaml secrets: licenseToken: "" modelApiKey: "" ``` 3. **Install.** ```sh helm dependency build charts/openbot helm install openbot charts/openbot \ --namespace openbot --create-namespace \ --values charts/openbot/ci/vanilla-values.yaml \ --values openbot-secrets.yaml \ --timeout 15m ``` 4. **Open your evaluation.** ```sh kubectl -n openbot get pods,jobs kubectl -n openbot port-forward svc/openbot-server 3001:3001 ``` Open . This configuration is single-user: anyone who can reach it is an administrator. Keep the port-forward local. The chart creates the runtime credentials, installs the databases, bootstraps Intelligence, and sets up the Learning container and scheduled jobs. Automatic Learning uses your model key too. For a team deployment, follow the [Helm guide](charts/openbot/README.md) to configure authentication, TLS, your database, secrets, persistent storage, and network policies. For a single-container alternative, see [Deploy it](#deploy-it). ## Run from source Use the template to customize the workspace, branding, Bots, and skills. The source setup below uses managed Intelligence by default; [local Intelligence](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) is also available. ```sh git clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot.git cd OpenBot ``` ### Requirements To run the open-source template locally, you’ll need the following. - Docker, for PostgreSQL and the shipped Bots. - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.4+, for the app, the API server and the tests (some tests fail on 1.3). - A CopilotKit Intelligence project and license. A free plan is available, and Intelligence can be self-hosted. - A model key. The proof-of-concept Bot uses OpenAI; the LangGraph Bot can use OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google. ### Quick start The example configuration sets `OPENBOT_SINGLE_USER=true`, so you can try the app as a local administrator. Configure [sign-in](#sign-in) before giving anyone else access. On a Mac, the free Developer plan also covers [running Intelligence locally](#intelligence-on-your-own-machine) with Docker. > **Setting up with an AI assistant?** Paste [`prompt.txt`](prompt.txt) into it first. It carries the > same steps as below plus the things that are easy to get wrong: which of the blank keys in > `.env.example` are actually yours to fill (the CopilotKit key and a model key), which the start > script fills for you, and what each start-up refusal means. Every claim in it is checked against > this repository. 1. Create `.env`: ```sh cp .env.example .env bun install ``` 2. Connect a fresh managed Intelligence project: ```sh npx --yes copilotkit@latest login npx --yes copilotkit@latest project select bun scripts/setup-learning.ts ``` The helper provisions the selected project's runtime key, creates or reuses its `openbot` Learning container, then writes both settings to `.env`. It preserves custom container assignments and never replaces an existing OpenBot key; with one set, it only creates `openbot` in that key's project if it is missing. For fresh self-hosted setup, set `INTELLIGENCE_API_URL` to that deployment's HTTPS API origin (or `http://localhost` for a local one) and run the helper without the two `npx` commands. It opens an isolated Chrome or Edge window for your usual sign-in and project choice; install either browser first. For CLI-managed local evaluation installs, it discovers the matching dashboard with the newest installed or cached CopilotKit CLI and uses that dashboard for login and session requests. Discovery runs offline with Bun, without downloading the CLI or requiring `npx` on your PATH. If no CLI is available, manually hosted deployments use their API origin for sign-in. Complete the local auth approval shown in the browser when prompted. The runtime API URL stays unchanged. It writes the API URL, the key and the container, not `INTELLIGENCE_GATEWAY_WS_URL`, so set that one to the same deployment yourself. Once `openbot` exists, the server assigns it as the default by itself unless [Admin → Automatic Learning](docs/automatic-learning.md) has a saved setting. Managed Intelligence needs no separate licence token. The same CopilotKit CLI sign-in provisions Composio automatically when you run `bash scripts/start.sh`. If that cannot complete, OpenBot still starts, with apps unavailable. You can run `bun run setup:composio` first to prepare it separately, or later to retry; it does not need a Learning container. The helper creates or reuses one isolated Composio project for this installation and saves its project key to `.env`. Existing Composio keys and Arcade configurations are preserved. Keep the private `.env.openbot-installation-id` file across restarts and interrupted setup attempts; do not copy it into a new installation. This needs a published CopilotKit CLI with `integrations composio provision` and the hosted provisioning service enabled. See [Composio setup](docs/plugins/composio.md#automatic-project-setup) for deployment preparation. 3. Fill the remaining required values: - `OPENAI_API_KEY` Keep the managed Intelligence URLs from `.env.example` unless you run Intelligence yourself. The example `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is public and fine locally; generate your own with: ```sh openssl rand -base64 32 ``` 4. Run: ```sh bash scripts/start.sh ``` 5. Open . `scripts/start.sh` starts Docker services, applies migrations, starts the API server on port 3001, starts the routine worker, starts the app on port 3010, and checks that the services answer their own health routes before printing next steps. `scripts/stop.sh` takes the same things down, including each Bot's computer, which compose does not own; `--keep-computers` leaves the computers running. Nothing is deleted: the database, the Bots' files and their browser profiles are volumes. ### On Windows Run the clone inside WSL 2 with Ubuntu, and run every step above from an Ubuntu terminal. [Windows (WSL 2)](docs/development.md#windows-wsl-2) lists what to install in Ubuntu first. Keep an Ubuntu terminal open while you use OpenBot, and open the app from your Windows browser at . ### Intelligence on your own machine To try Intelligence on one Mac instead of the managed service, follow [Evaluate Intelligence locally](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/self-hosting-local). The free [Developer plan](https://www.copilotkit.ai/pricing) qualifies. The local licence lasts 30 days and `npx copilotkit@latest local renew` renews it as often as you need, while your account is in good standing.
